stimuli.text: A block of mass 5 kg on a 30° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 7 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.25. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.7 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.13\cos(4t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A solid sphere (I = ⅖MR²) and a hoop (I = MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 2.2 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 2x^3$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 2$$ m to $$x = 5$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: A 0.3 kg ball hits a wall at 19 m/s and rebounds at 3 m/s. The contact lasts 0.05 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.
The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -100x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: ω is the square root of the coefficient.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 460 kg load 21 m at constant speed in 13 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A curve of radius 120 m is banked so that a car at 22 m/s needs no friction. What is the banking angle?

options.why: Measure the angle from the horizontal.
Use tan θ = v²/(rg), from dividing the force components.

questions.stem: A car moving at 16 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 7 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.
That is the stopping time in seconds.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 40° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.25. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
The component along the incline is mg sin θ.
Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).

questions.stem: A planet has 0.5 times Earth's mass and 4 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)
A boat points straight across a river 40 m wide, moving at 6 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 1 m/s. How long does the crossing take?

options.why: The perpendicular component alone sets the crossing time.
The current is perpendicular to the heading.
The current is perpendicular to the heading.
Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 1.5 m high at 2 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
Take the square root for the time.
Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.

questions.stem: Masses of 4 kg and 3 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the tension in the string?

options.why: The lighter mass accelerates up, so T exceeds its weight.
The heavier mass accelerates down, so T is less than its weight.

questions.stem: A 78 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating downward at 3 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: The acceleration changes the normal force.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
Check the direction of the acceleration.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 2x^2$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 1$$ m to $$x = 4$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 48 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 18 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.

questions.stem: A uniform 3 m beam weighing 300 N rests on supports at both ends. A 800 N load sits 1 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Include the beam's weight at its center.
That is the left support's force.
The load is not at the center.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 2t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 5 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its position at $$t = 4$$ s?

options.why: Correct. Integrate twice, using the initial conditions.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum is 1.2 m long. What is its period for small oscillations?
A spring with $$k = 360$$ N/m is compressed 0.11 m and launches a 0.6 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 5$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^2$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.09\cos(5t)$$ m. What is its maximum speed?
Two springs with constants 100 N/m and 50 N/m are connected in series and support a 4 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: The force is the weight, mg.
Series and parallel rules are reversed.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 4x^3 - 27x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 12x² − 27 = 0 gives x = 1.5 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A thin spherical shell rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 2 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ⅔MR².
That is only correct for a hoop.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 4 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?
A planet has mass $$2 \times 10^{25}$$ kg and radius $$2 \times 10^{7}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 26 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its maximum height?

options.why: Use the vertical component, v₀ sin θ.
Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 20.8 m/s, v₀y = 15.6 m/s. H = v₀y²/(2g) = 12.5 m.

questions.stem: A 4 kg cart moving at 7 m/s collides with and sticks to a 6 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.
Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.

questions.explanation: v_f = 4·7/10 = 2.8 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 58.8 J.

questions.stem: A 2 kg ball moving at +8 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 5 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 5 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: That would be a sticking collision.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -3.43 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 4.57 m/s.

questions.stem: A 4 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 1 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.
The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 8.71 m/s².

questions.stem: A 8 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 6 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.2. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Both blocks accelerate; divide by the total mass.
Include friction on the table block.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.

questions.stem: An object of mass 1.9 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.06$$ kg/s. What is its terminal speed?

options.why: Drag here is linear in v.
Correct. At terminal speed, mg = bv.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 310 m/s and τ = m/b = 31.7 s.

questions.stem: A constant torque of 17 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 0.2$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 1 revolution. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 9 rad/s and amplitude 0.15 m. What is its speed when it is 0.03 m from equilibrium?

options.why: That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Use A² − x² under a square root.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.
Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 9 m down a 30° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.3. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.

questions.stem: A 2500 kg car heading east at 20 m/s collides with a 1500 kg car heading north at 10 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.
Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Weight each velocity by its mass.

questions.stem: A 4 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 9t^2$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.
Divide by the mass to get speed.

questions.explanation: J = ∫F dt = 192 N·s; v = J/m = 48 m/s.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 2.8 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 6 kg and radius 0.6 m spins at 14 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 1.25 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.

questions.stem: What is the rotational inertia of a uniform rod of mass 6 kg and length 4 m about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod?

options.why: Correct. I = ML²/3 (parallel-axis theorem from ML²/12).
The mass is spread along the rod.

questions.stem: A 10 g bullet moving at 340 m/s embeds in a 2.1 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Find the block's speed after the collision first.
Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.

questions.explanation: V = 1.61 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.132 m.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 5 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 1.5 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.13 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
